questions.question: According to the lesson, what is the single most important thing that carries you from 'I finished a course' to 'a developer who keeps building'?
options: Watching more advanced tutorials
Reps — building things where nobody hands you the next line
Memorizing the names of 20 popular libraries
Waiting until you have time for one big project
questions.explanation: The lesson says the thing that carries you forward isn't another tutorial, it's reps — building things where nobody hands you the next line.

questions.question: Per the learn-when-needed principle, what is the right trigger to finally learn Tailwind CSS?
options: Everyone online says Tailwind is great
It's currently the most popular styling tool
You're sick of writing the same CSS and your stylesheets are a mess
A new project is starting and you want the latest tools
questions.explanation: The lesson states the annoyance — being sick of rewriting the same CSS with messy stylesheets — is the trigger, not the hype.

questions.question: From the 'reach for this when…' menu, when should you reach for TanStack Query (React Query)?
options: When manual fetch plus loading and caching state gets painful and repetitive across components
When you want routing, server rendering, and a backend in one framework
When you want the classic Node backend with the biggest tutorial pool
When hand-writing CSS keeps slowing you down
questions.explanation: The menu says to reach for TanStack Query when manual fetch plus loading and caching state is getting painful and repetitive across your components.

questions.question: How does the lesson distinguish Hono from Express in the tool menu?
options: Hono adds server rendering and routing in one framework; Express is styling-focused
Hono is a lightweight modern backend and a good first 'real backend'; Express is the classic Node backend with the biggest tutorial pool
Hono replaces React's data fetching; Express replaces your CSS
Hono is only for frontends; Express is only for databases
questions.explanation: The menu describes Hono as a lightweight, modern backend and good first 'real backend', and Express as the classic Node backend with the biggest tutorial pool.

questions.question: What momentum tactic does the lesson recommend for surviving off-weeks and ADHD?
options: Commit to one ambitious app and work on it for six months
Rely on willpower to push through the off-weeks
Ship something small every month and build in public
Add three new tools at once to stay challenged
questions.explanation: The lesson advises lowering the bar by shipping something small every month and building in public so the wins are visible and there's a tiny external deadline.
